# Rootwall

> Rootwall is a membership scheme that administers accountability for API traffic between two
> named companies, including traffic generated by AI agents. It is a scheme in the sense that a
> card scheme is a scheme: a published rulebook, an admission standard, an evidence standard and
> a consequence. It is not a network, a gateway, an identity provider or a security product, and
> no traffic passes through it.

Rootwall is operated from the United Kingdom. The rulebook is published in full and is governed by
the law of England and Wales. Membership commences 1 April 2027 at the earliest. As of August 2026
the scheme has no members and no session has been conducted under its rules.

Note on the name: rootwall.ai is a governance scheme for B2B API and agent traffic. It is not a
ratings, scoring or reputation product, and it publishes no rating, ranking or reputation index of
any kind. Any earlier or unrelated use of the name "Rootwall" is a different thing.

## What it does

- Admits a member once against a published standard, rather than each counterparty assessing it
  separately.
- Receives, from BOTH parties to a session independently, short signed records of what happened:
  who, under whose delegated authority, against which declared scope, with what outcome.
- Reconciles the two records. Agreement is recorded as a matched pair, which is a positive record
  that nothing went wrong. Disagreement puts both parties on notice.
- Determines whether a published rule was broken, by comparison and not by inference.
- Attaches a consequence: a change of standing, and sometimes a sum fixed in advance.
- Releases the signed records to both members at once when loss is in dispute, taking no position.

## What it deliberately does not do

- It is never in the data path and never a counterparty to anything.
- It never receives payloads, argument values or any member's logs. Records carry argument names
  and a digest of their values, never the values.
- It never determines loss, never arbitrates, never underwrites, and never scores or ranks anyone.
- It issues no identity. It consumes existing mechanisms such as SPIFFE, Web Bot Auth and MCP-I.

## Who enforces a consequence, since this is the most commonly asked question

Money moves between the two companies and never through Rootwall. Rootwall does not collect, hold,
route or take a share of any sum. Rootwall's own enforcement is standing: not paying is itself a
breach and suspends the member, and revocation propagates within one business day to every member
that accepted that scope class. Recovery of the money itself is an ordinary contract claim between
the two companies, using the signed records Rootwall releases to both sides. Nobody can compel
payment; the rulebook states this in its own Known limitations as "exit is the floor of
enforceability".

## Pages

- [Front page](https://rootwall.ai/): what the scheme is, who it is for, and what it is not.
- [The rulebook](https://rootwall.ai/rulebook): the full text, version 1.0, in force. Nine parts,
  37 clauses, five schedules, with known limitations stated in the document. Every clause has its
  own address, for example https://rootwall.ai/rulebook#22.3, and numbering is stable.
- [Common questions](https://rootwall.ai/questions): enforcement, what happens if a member leaves,
  what the scheme can see, how it differs from identity products, cost, and what does not yet exist.
- [Schedule of fees](https://rootwall.ai/fees): version 1.0. $6,000 a year in the receiving role,
  $1,000 in the emitting role, $350 admission either side, $1,200 per scope class assessment.
- [The survey](https://rootwall.ai/hundred-platforms): version 1.0, published 2 September 2026.
  What roughly one hundred UK and EU software platforms require of third parties calling their
  APIs, read from primary source on 28 August 2026. Almost all have a gate; seven publish a partner
  rulebook; none holds a record of what a third party actually did, the furthest any of them goes
  being a right to inspect at the platform's discretion. Peppol, the best-governed network in the
  sample, requires its providers to log everything, keep it three months and reveal it on request,
  and that is still a log. Every document quoted is linked to an archived copy taken on the day it
  was read. Numbered points are separately citable, for example
  https://rootwall.ai/hundred-platforms#p63.
- [Version history](https://rootwall.ai/history): every published version of the rulebook, the
  fee schedule and the survey, with dates.
